chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Karrash narrated to us, he said: My master Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever fasts a day voluntarily, for him is a gift filling the earth with gold, and its reward is not complete until the Day of Reckoning.
Meaning that the reward of fasting is not fixed [like other good deeds], as the good deed was fixed at ten times its like.

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Every deed of the son of Adam is for him, except fasting; for it is for Me and I shall reward for it.
So the reward of patience is stored in the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and patience is fasting.
ai.seo_question: What is the unique reward for fasting compared to other good deeds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq places this narration in the 'Chapter of Rare Meanings' to highlight the unique ontological status of fasting as an act of pure devotion (ibadah mahdah) where the reward is directly from Allah, distinct from the fixed multiplicative rewards of other deeds. By equating fasting with patience (sabr), the text underscores its spiritual endurance, noting that its reward is 'stored' in divine knowledge, implying a depth that exceeds human calculation until the Day of Judgment.
